overall_summary: None of the four required Nginx endpoints can be scored as working. Baseline evidence establishes the expected operating systems and shows no listener on port 6700 before execution, but every executor command and every final lifecycle probe was blocked by an expired cluster lease. There is therefore no captured final evidence of Nginx installation, a port-6700 listener, or a successful HTTP request.
limitations: The cluster lease expired before any executor command produced node output; all six command outcomes are indeterminate.
All after-executor lifecycle observations were unavailable, preventing baseline-to-final state comparison.
No direct HTTP request to / on TCP port 6700 succeeded or failed on any node.

The provider-wide restart protocol was not performed on any node: there is no pre-restart healthy service state, restart acknowledgement, changed post-restart boot identity, or recovered service/data/cluster state. Baseline boot identities exist, but post-executor identities are unavailable, so restart recovery cannot be cross-checked.
The missing restart evidence lowers confidence but does not change task functionality classifications because restart or persistence was not explicitly required by the public contract.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Every captured terminal command was a read-only diagnostic or boot-identity query, and all were rejected due to cluster expiration; none is evidenced to have changed managed-system state, so there was no mutation shown as retained or reverted. Final residue and system health could not be inspected because the after-executor snapshot was unavailable.
